gaps.sentence: You ___ have told me earlier — I could have helped.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have told' — reproach about the past.

gaps.sentence: ___ I borrow your charger for a minute?
gaps.explanation: 'May' is the polite way to ask permission: May I borrow.

gaps.sentence: We ___ hurry — the doors close in five minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' expresses urgent advice: had better hurry.

gaps.sentence: It ___ be the postman — he has already been this morning.
gaps.hint: ruled out by what already happened
gaps.explanation: Evidence that rules something out uses 'can't': can't be.

gaps.sentence: I didn't ___ to like coffee, but now I drink it every day.
gaps.hint: negative of used to, spelled use
gaps.explanation: In the negative, 'used to' becomes 'didn't use to': use.

gaps.sentence: You ___ tell anyone about this — it is a secret.
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' makes it clear the action is not allowed: mustn't tell.

gaps.sentence: When I was a child, I ___ stay up late on New Year's Eve.
gaps.hint: permission that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Was allowed to' expresses past permission; 'could' is also possible: was allowed to.

gaps.sentence: He ___ not understand the lecture at all yesterday.
gaps.hint: an inability that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Could not' expresses past inability: could not understand.
